strong.text:
Yeon: Strong chart. You work at one speed: full. Then you're surprised nobody else is at full.

Bom: You get things done that others give up on.

Yeon: You also send follow-ups to your follow-ups.

This week, before you jump in, ask one question: "What does done look like for you?" Saves you redoing someone else's version of done.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You don't work hard. You work loud. Everyone can hear the keyboard.

weak.text:
Bom: Your chart runs soft. You work best with the right people around you, and you notice every mood in the office.

Yeon: Which is lovely, and also why one passive-aggressive email ruins your afternoon.

Bom: Your sensitivity is data. Not a weakness.

Protect one quiet hour a day. Notifications off. That's where your best work actually happens.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One quiet hour a day. That's where you shine.

strong.text:
With a strong chart you lead before anyone asks. Sometimes before anyone wanted a leader.

Yeon: You fill every silence with your own idea. Second three, there it is.

Bom: End meetings with "What am I missing?" and wait through the awkward pause.

The best idea in the room often shows up after second seven. You've just never waited that long.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: "What am I missing?" Then shut up for seven seconds.

weak.text:
With a light chart you might not call yourself a leader. People come to you anyway.

Bom: You lead by example, attention and care. That counts. It often lasts longer than leading by command.

Yeon: So stop doing the job without the title. Ask for the title when the work is already yours.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: They already follow you. Ask for the title that matches.

strong.text:
Strong charts take over a team without meaning to. You talk first, decide fast and move on.

Yeon: Meanwhile the quiet colleague is still on slide two of their thoughts.

Bom: Make room on purpose. Ask the quiet person by name. Let people disagree with you in writing.

Better ideas. Fewer silent grudges by the coffee machine.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Ask the quiet colleague by name. Their idea might be the good one.

weak.text:
Light charts become the team's peacekeeper. And its dumping ground.

Yeon: You're easy to ask, so everyone asks. Including people from other floors.

Bom: Say "Let me check my week first" before agreeing to anything.

It isn't rude. It's how people learn your time has value.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Before any yes: check the week. Out loud.

strong.text:
Strong charts burn out late and hard. You can push through the early warnings for months.

Yeon: You won't believe it's burnout until your body or your temper sends a formal letter.

Bom: Schedule recovery like a meeting. A holiday is part of the job, not a prize for finishing it.

Because the job is never finished.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Holiday goes in the calendar first. Work fits around it.

weak.text:
Light charts burn out earlier and more often. You also notice sooner, which is a real advantage.

Bom: Act on the first signs instead of waiting to be sure.

Yeon: One quiet day at the first wave of exhaustion saves you three weeks later. The maths is brutal.

Your sensitivity is an early warning system. Trust it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Early tired is a signal, not a flaw. Act on ring one.

strong.text:
With a strong chart, too much hand-holding feels like a cage with a nice carpet.

Bom: You tend to do best with real authority and real challenge. Own outcomes. Have a say in strategy. See your impact.

Yeon: Then pick a team that'll tell you honestly when you're steamrolling. You won't notice on your own.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Own the outcome. Keep one colleague who'll tell you the truth.

weak.text:
With a light chart, the culture matters as much as the role.

Bom: A great job in a harsh workplace will drain you. A modest job with kind, competent people lets you grow fast.

Yeon: In interviews, ask how the team handles mistakes. The answer is the real job description.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: How they treat mistakes tells you how they'll treat you.

peer_strong.text:
You'd rather have a rival than a boss. Honestly, you'd rather have neither.

Your chart is stacked with {dm_el}, your own element. Saju calls that the peer family: colleagues, competitors, partners.

Yeon: You measure yourself against peers. Equal credit, equal treatment, or you'll notice.

Bom: You're brilliant in partnerships of equals and fiercely self-reliant.

Yeon: Taking direction from someone you don't respect? Visible pain. Share credit generously, and let others lead sometimes without counting it as a loss.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Own element everywhere. Share the credit anyway. It costs less than you think.

output_strong.text:
You've rewritten a process nobody asked you to rewrite. It was better. Nobody thanked you.

Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} produces. Saju calls it output: creativity, expression, skill.

Bom: You're the maker. The ideas person. The one with a talent people notice.

Yeon: Bureaucracy makes you itch. And you criticise authority a little too openly in the group chat.

Bom: Channel it into building better systems instead of mocking the old ones.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're the maker. Build the better system, skip the roast.

wealth_strong.text:
You think in deliverables. Even your weekends have milestones.

Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} controls. Saju calls it wealth: resources, results, management.

Bom: Budgets, logistics, turning plans into outcomes. You like being measured on what you achieve.

Yeon: The shadow: treating people like line items.

Bom: The spreadsheet has humans in it. Ask how they are before you ask where the numbers are.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Results matter. So do the people making them.

power_strong.text:
You've read the employee handbook. All of it. Voluntarily.

Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element that controls your {dm_el}. Saju calls it power: authority, structure, responsibility.

Bom: On a strong chart that's the natural manager. You understand hierarchy and carry serious responsibility well.

Yeon: The shadow is rigidity. Taking work so seriously you forget it's allowed to be fun.

Bom: Leave room for the unexpected. Some of the best things at work weren't on the plan.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Born manager. Schedule some fun. Yes, schedule it, you'll only do it then.

resource_strong.text:
You've done the research. You've done more research. The draft is still not sent.

Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element that feeds your {dm_el}. Saju calls it resource: knowledge, learning, support.

Bom: You're the expert. The person who understands the theory behind everything.

Yeon: And you wait too long to act because there's always one more thing to read.

Bom: Ship the draft. Your knowledge is worth most when it reaches people.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: The expert. Send it before it's perfect.

output_weak.text:
You help everyone. You produce loads. And by Thursday there's nothing left in the tank.

Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} produces: effort, expression, output.

Yeon: On a light chart that's the overworker pattern. Talent real. Battery finite. Hours infinite, apparently.

Bom: Measure your work by impact, not hours.

Yeon: Stop when the important part is done. The unimportant part can wait until never.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Impact, not hours. Close the laptop when the real part's done.

wealth_weak.text:
You've somehow become responsible for three budgets and another team's problems. Nobody remembers deciding that.

Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} controls. Old saju books call it wealth heavy, self light: a lot to manage, not much backup.

Bom: You end up holding more than your role or your stamina can carry.

Yeon: Ask for resources before you accept responsibility.

Bom: "I can take that on if I get help with X" is a completely professional sentence.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ask for help before you say yes, not after.

power_weak.text:
Every email from your boss feels like a performance review.

Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element that presses on your {dm_el}: pressure, authority, rules.

Bom: You're conscientious and reliable. Criticism from above lands very heavily.

Yeon: Like working under permanent inspection, by an inspector who lives in your head.

Bom: Look for managers who are clear and kind, on purpose. Keep proof of your good work for the days the inner critic gets loud.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: The inspector in your head has never once done your job. Ignore the report.

rooted_on_paper.text:
Bom: At work this looks like someone confident in the meeting who rereads their own email three times after.

Yeon: Colleagues think you've got it handled. Some days you do. Some days it's willpower and a third coffee.

Both are real. Choose roles where support is built in, a good manager, a strong team, and stop expecting yourself to look fine every single day.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Confident in the room, rereading the email after. Both are you.

output_strong.text:
{miss_el} is missing from your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's the output element: how work becomes visible.

Yeon: You do great work, move on and tell nobody. Then act surprised at review time.

Bom: Borrow some output. A short weekly update. A demo. One sentence in the team meeting about what you finished.

Yeon: Next page: your coworkers. They have opinions about you. Some are even nice.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Great work nobody sees doesn't show up at reviews. Send the update.

wealth_strong.text:
{miss_el} is missing from your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's the wealth element: the pull toward measurable results.

Bom: You care about the work itself more than where it leads. Lovely.

Yeon: Until reviews come around and you have nothing to point at.

Bom: Set one concrete target a quarter. Then turn the page: your coworkers, and what they say when you're not there.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: One target per quarter. Something you can point at.

power_strong.text:
{miss_el} is missing from your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's the power element: structure and authority.

Yeon: You resist being managed. Hierarchies make you itchy.

Bom: Build your own structure instead. Deadlines you set. A mentor you chose. Rules you'd actually follow.

Yeon: Next page: coworkers. Including the one who keeps sending calendar invites.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: No frame built in? Build your own. Deadlines you picked.

resource_strong.text:
{miss_el} is missing from your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's the resource element: learning and support.

Bom: You push forward on talent and drive and rarely stop to learn or ask for help.

Yeon: Talent with no top-ups runs out eventually.

Bom: Book learning like a meeting. A course, a mentor, a book a month. Next page: the colleagues who could help, if you let them.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: A book a month, one mentor. Talent needs feeding too.

output_weak.text:
{miss_el} is missing from your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's the output element: expression.

Bom: It protects a light chart from overworking. Good.

Yeon: It also keeps your ideas locked in your head, where they win zero arguments.

Bom: Share one idea a week, in writing, with your name on it. Then next page: your coworkers.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your ideas need daylight. Sign them.

wealth_weak.text:
{miss_el} is missing from your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's the wealth element: chasing results.

Bom: You don't push for the promotion, the project or the raise. It keeps you calm.

Yeon: It also keeps you overlooked.

Bom: Ask for one thing a year, clearly and in advance. Next page, the coworkers who might be getting what you didn't ask for.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One clear ask a year. Made early.

power_weak.text:
{miss_el} is missing from your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's the power element: outside pressure.

Bom: Fewer rules weighing on you. Good for your nerves.

Yeon: Less good for knowing what you're meant to do on a Wednesday.

Bom: Ask for a clear role, written priorities and a manager who spells out expectations. Next page: the people you'd be asking.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Ask for priorities in writing. Clarity is kindness, for you especially.

resource_weak.text:
{miss_el} is missing from your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's the resource element: support and learning.

Yeon: You're working on willpower with no backup. Impressive. Unsustainable.

Bom: Build your support on purpose. One mentor. One colleague you trust. One learning habit that refills you.

Yeon: Next page: your coworkers. One of them could be the colleague you trust.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Mentor, ally, refill habit. Build the backup on purpose.

none_strong.text:
All five elements turn up in your pillars. On a strong chart that's range: manage, create, analyse, lead.

Yeon: The trap: good at everything, known for nothing.

Bom: Pick the one skill you want people to name when they describe you. Sharpen it on purpose.

Yeon: Next page: what your coworkers would currently say. Brace.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Good at everything, famous for nothing. Pick your one thing.

none_weak.text:
All five elements turn up in your pillars. On a light chart that's flexibility. You fit almost any team.

Bom: Don't let flexible turn into overlooked.

Yeon: Choose the work you want more of. Say it, out loud, to the person who hands it out.

Bom: Next page: your coworkers, and where you fit among them.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Tell whoever hands out work what you want more of.

resource.title: What refills you at work: {helper_el} (non-negotiable)
resource.text:
Every chart has one element that brings it back into balance. For your light {dm_el} chart it's {helper_el}, the element that feeds you.

Bom: At work that means mentors, learning, supportive managers and real rest.

Yeon: You do your best work after you've been taught and looked after. So pick places where that's the culture, not a perk on a slide.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your refill is {helper_el}: mentors, learning, rest that's real.

peer.title: What keeps you steady at work: {helper_el}, your own element
peer.text:
Every chart has one element that brings it back into balance. Yours already has plenty of nourishment on paper, so what steadies you is your own element, {helper_el}.

Bom: At work that means peers. A work friend. A project partner. Colleagues at your level you can be honest with.

Yeon: Find your people at work. They're worth more than any perk.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your steadying element is {helper_el}: one real work friend.

output.title: Where all that extra drive belongs: {helper_el}
output.text:
Every chart has one element that brings it back into balance. A strong {dm_el} chart needs an outlet, and yours is {helper_el}, the element you produce.

Bom: At work that means making things. Building, writing, designing, teaching.

Yeon: Drive with no outlet turns into micromanagement and office politics. We've all met that person. Don't become them.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your outlet is {helper_el}. Make something, or you'll start managing people too hard.

wealth.title: What keeps you balanced at work: {helper_el}
wealth.text:
Every chart has one element that brings it back into balance. Yours is strong and already expressive, so what balances you is {helper_el}, the element you shape.

Bom: At work that means concrete goals and measurable results. A target. A budget. A launch date.

Yeon: Aim it at something you can finish. "Ongoing" is not a goal.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your balance is {helper_el}: a goal with an end date.

wood.text: Wood, office version: a growth plan, one new skill a year, mentoring someone, a desk near a window or at least a plant.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Wood for you: something to grow, someone to teach, a desk plant.

fire.text: Fire, office version: visibility, presenting your work, energetic teammates, celebrating wins, natural light.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Fire for you: present your work and celebrate the win out loud.

earth.text: Earth, office version: routine, a stable team, a clear role, a real lunch break and a workspace that feels like yours.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Earth for you: routine, real lunch, a desk that's yours.

metal.text: Metal, office version: clear priorities, tidy systems, saying no to low-value tasks, finishing things completely.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Metal for you: clear priorities and a polite no to the fluff.

water.text: Water, office version: thinking time, flexible hours, research, travel, quiet corners and room to explore ideas.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Water for you: thinking time and a quiet corner.

rat.text:
You know who really makes decisions in this building. It isn't who the org chart says.

Your day branch shows the private you that close colleagues eventually meet. Yours is the Rat, 子, midnight Water: resourceful, quick, observant, good with side doors.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rat underneath: you know who actually decides. And you're not telling.

ox.text:
Three reorgs, two new CEOs, one rebrand. Still here. Still doing excellent work.

Your day branch shows the private you that close colleagues eventually meet. Yours is the Ox, 丑, cold wet Earth: patient, enduring, stubborn.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ox underneath: you outlast every reorg and every flashy hire.

tiger.text:
Your hand is the first one up for the scary project.

Your day branch shows the private you that close colleagues eventually meet. Yours is the Tiger, 寅, early spring Wood: bold, restless, protective of your team.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Tiger underneath: volunteers for the terrifying thing. Every time.

rabbit.text:
You'd rewrite an email nine times to avoid one open argument.

Your day branch shows the private you that close colleagues eventually meet. Yours is the Rabbit, 卯, spring Wood: diplomatic, tasteful, allergic to conflict.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rabbit underneath: you make the office nicer, and dodge every fight in it.

dragon.text:
There's a plan in your head that's bigger than your current job. You've told maybe two people.

Your day branch shows the private you that close colleagues eventually meet. Yours is the Dragon, 辰, damp Earth storing Water: ambitious, imaginative, more complex than your work persona.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Dragon underneath: big private plans, strictly need-to-know.

snake.text:
You read office politics like a novel. You rarely reveal your next move.

Your day branch shows the private you that close colleagues eventually meet. Yours is the Snake, 巳, early summer Fire: strategic, perceptive, discreet.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Snake underneath: three moves ahead in every meeting. Quietly.

horse.text:
Desk job with no variety? Twitchy by 11am.

Your day branch shows the private you that close colleagues eventually meet. Yours is the Horse, 午, midsummer Fire: energetic, independent, impatient.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Horse underneath: you've walked to the kitchen six times since lunch.

goat.text:
A harsh office shrinks you. A gentle one and suddenly you're the most creative person there.

Your day branch shows the private you that close colleagues eventually meet. Yours is the Goat, 未, warm late-summer Earth: creative, kind, sensitive to atmosphere.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Goat underneath: gentle offices make you bloom. Choose them.

monkey.text:
There's a shortcut for every process. You've found most of them. Some are probably not allowed.

Your day branch shows the private you that close colleagues eventually meet. Yours is the Monkey, 申, early autumn Metal: clever, inventive, easily bored.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Monkey underneath: you automated your job and didn't tell anyone.

rooster.text:
Your work is meticulous. You notice, instantly, when someone else's isn't.

Your day branch shows the private you that close colleagues eventually meet. Yours is the Rooster, 酉, autumn Metal: precise, proud, detail-obsessed.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rooster underneath: you've silently fixed other people's spacing.

dog.text:
You'll stand up for a colleague being treated unfairly, even when it costs you.

Your day branch shows the private you that close colleagues eventually meet. Yours is the Dog, 戌, dry autumn Earth: loyal, principled, protective.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Dog underneath: you'd defend a coworker against the CEO. You have.

pig.text:
You share credit freely and assume good intentions. People love you for it. A few take advantage.

Your day branch shows the private you that close colleagues eventually meet. Yours is the Pig, 亥, early winter Water: generous, easygoing, honest.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Pig underneath: you hand out credit like snacks. Save one for you.

day_branch_heading: The work self only close colleagues meet: the {day_animal} ({day_branch})

student.text:
You're still studying. Which means your work style is already leaking out in group projects.

Bom: Notice which group projects light you up and which ones you dread. That pattern tends to follow you into your first job.

Yeon: The one where you did everything and still let Jordan present? Data.

Bom: Try one internship or project in a field from the job chapter later on, just to test it.

Yeon: And start a log of projects you loved. It becomes your first portfolio and your first honest map.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Group projects are data. Notice which ones you'd do again.

early.text:
Early career. You learn the most and control the least. Fun.

Bom: Pick bosses more carefully than you pick companies. A great first manager teaches more in a year than three courses.

Yeon: Keep a list of what you enjoy and what drains you. It'll steer your next move better than any salary table.

Bom: Say yes to stretch tasks that teach you something.

Yeon: Say no to the ones that only teach you how to be tired.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Pick the boss more carefully than the logo. Seriously.

mid.text:
A few years in. Your strengths are visible now. So are your habits.

Bom: Good moment to shape the role around what you do best, not what you fell into.

Yeon: Tell your manager which parts of the job you'd like more of. They can't read your mind. They can barely read their inbox.

Bom: Find a mentor two steps ahead. One lunch a quarter is plenty.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Shape the role now. Ask for more of the parts you're best at.

lead.text:
You lead people. Which means your habits are now multiplied by everyone on your team.

Yeon: Your bad Monday is now eight people's bad Monday.

Bom: Read the leadership chapter twice. Then ask one person you trust what it's actually like to work for you.

Yeon: Their answer beats any reading. Including this one.

Bom: And keep learning yourself. Leaders who stop learning start managing on autopilot.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your mood is the team's forecast. Ask them what the weather's like.

between.text:
Between jobs. Uncomfortable. Also a rare chance to choose on purpose.

Bom: Use the job chapter as a filter, not a rulebook.

Yeon: Before the next interview, write down three conditions for your best work. Team, pace, boss. Ask about each. You're interviewing them too.

Bom: Keep a daily rhythm in the meantime. Structure keeps confidence from leaking away.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Team, pace, boss. Interview them back on all three.

unsaid.text:
You skipped where you are. Fair. This bit works for anyone.

Bom: Student, mid-career, leading, between things. Your work style shows up the same way: in what fills you up and what drains you.

Yeon: Keep both lists. They're more useful than any job title.

Bom: Add a third if you like: what you'd do even if nobody paid you. It often points somewhere useful.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Two lists: what fills you up, what drains you. Start tonight.

meetings.text:
You said meetings drain you. Translation: you need time to actually do the work, and talking about it feels like a tax.

Bom: Protect two focus blocks a week and treat them like client meetings.

Yeon: Ask for agendas. Offer to answer by email. Leave meetings where you're not needed. People will secretly admire it.

Bom: If you run meetings, cut them to twenty-five minutes. Instant fan club.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Two focus blocks a week. Defend them like a client is waiting.

unclear.text:
You said unclear goals drain you. You'll commit to anything once someone says what success looks like.

Yeon: So ask, explicitly: "What does done look like, and how will we know it worked?"

Bom: If nobody can answer, write your own definition and send it round. People are usually relieved.

Yeon: Unclear goals hide unclear priorities. Ask which two things matter most this month.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: "What does done look like?" Ask it every single time.

people.text:
You said difficult people drain you. Everyone hates them, but for you they're the main cost of the job.

Bom: Which says you care about the human side a lot.

Yeon: Pick one difficult person. Change one thing: the channel, the timing, the length.

Bom: Small adjustments fix more than big confrontations.

Yeon: And keep one ally in the building. One friendly face changes how heavy everyone else feels.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Change the channel, the timing or the length. Small fixes work.

boredom.text:
You said boredom drains you. Same thing every day, and your brain files a complaint.

Bom: You need novelty and growth to stay switched on.

Yeon: Ask for one stretch project a year. Learn something next door to your role. Redesign a boring process until it runs itself.

Bom: Boredom is information. It usually means you've outgrown something.

Yeon: Until then, add variety at the edges. New route, new lunch spot, a side project.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Bored means outgrown. Ask for the stretch project.

unsaid.text:
You didn't say what drains you. Fair, it changes week to week.

Bom: Next time you get home exhausted, write down the one thing that took the most out of you.

Yeon: A month of notes will beat this paragraph. Patterns show up fast on paper.

Bom: Most people are surprised what tops the list.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Every tired evening, one line: what drained you most.

wood.heading: What you need at work: room to grow
wood.text:
Bom: You need to feel you're getting somewhere. A new skill, a bigger project, a next step.

Yeon: Stagnation makes you update your CV in the toilets.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Tell your manager where you want to grow. Out loud.

fire.heading: What you need at work: to be seen
fire.text:
Yeon: You need your work noticed. Not credited in a footnote. Noticed.

Bom: Recognition is fuel for you. Ask for feedback, not just tasks.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your work deserves a spotlight. Ask for the meeting slot.

earth.heading: What you need at work: stability
earth.text:
Bom: You need clear expectations and a steady rhythm. Then you're the most reliable person in the building.

Yeon: Constant reorgs make you quietly furious. And quietly job-hunting.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ask what's expected. You'll exceed it every time.

metal.heading: What you need at work: standards
metal.text:
Yeon: You need things done properly. Clear rules, fair process, nobody cutting corners.

Bom: Sloppy work around you feels personal. It isn't. But your standards are a gift.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You can spot a broken process from orbit.

water.heading: What you need at work: freedom to think
water.text:
Bom: You need space to think in your own way. Flexible time, big problems, freedom to connect the dots.

Yeon: Micromanagement makes you go silent. Then you go to a competitor.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Give you the problem, not the steps.

peer.heading: Your leadership superpower
peer.text:
Your chart's loudest element is your own, so your tool is partnership.

Bom: First among equals. Shared decisions, a team of strong peers, colleagues instead of subordinates.

Yeon: Hire people who are better than you at something. Then tell them. Out loud. It'll hurt a bit.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Partnership is your tool. Hire people better than you at something.

output.heading: Your leadership superpower
output.text:
Your chart's loudest element is the one you produce, so your tool is inspiration.

Bom: You lead with ideas and the way you talk about the work. People follow the vision.

Yeon: Pair it with someone who loves process. Otherwise the vision stays a beautiful speech with no Monday.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Inspiration is your tool. Get a co-pilot who adores checklists.

wealth.heading: Your leadership superpower
wealth.text:
Your chart's loudest element is the one you control, so your tool is execution.

Bom: Resources organised, targets set, results delivered. Teams under you ship.

Yeon: Make sure they know why it matters. Results feel better with a reason stapled to them.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Execution is your tool. Staple a reason to every target.

power.heading: Your leadership superpower
power.text:
Your chart's loudest element is the one that presses on you, so your tool is structure.

Bom: Clear roles, fair rules, accountability. People always know where they stand.

Yeon: Add flexibility where it costs nothing. Rules that bend for good reasons earn more respect than rules made of concrete.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Structure is your tool. Let it bend when the reason is good.

resource.heading: Your leadership superpower
resource.text:
Your chart's loudest element is the one that feeds you, so your tool is mentoring.

Bom: You teach, explain and develop people. Your team learns loads under you.

Yeon: Remember to decide, too. A brilliant explanation is not the same as making the call.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Mentoring is your tool. Teaching doesn't replace deciding.

peer.heading: The coworker you are
peer.text:
Yeon: You're the equal. Fair, independent, and you notice instantly if credit or workload isn't split evenly.

Bom: People trust you to be straight with them.

Watch the competitive edge with colleagues at your level. Most of them are on your side.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You know exactly who did what on that project. Most of them are allies.

output.heading: The coworker you are
output.text:
Bom: You're the creative spark. Fun in brainstorms. The reason the team chat is worth reading.

Yeon: Also the reason three ideas from March are still "in progress".

Make sure your ideas come with an offer to help build them.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Brainstorm star. Stay for the building part.

wealth.heading: The coworker you are
wealth.text:
Yeon: You're the organiser. Shared tracker, clear next steps, the reminder email nobody wanted but everyone needed.

Bom: Teams run better with you in them.

Sometimes people feel managed by a peer. Ask before you assign.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You assigned your manager a task. Bold. Ask first next time.

power.heading: The coworker you are
power.text:
Bom: You're the reliable one. Punctual, careful, true to your word. People bring you the important stuff.

Yeon: You can seem a bit serious. Your emojis are all thumbs up.

A joke in the team chat now and then shows the human side.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One joke in the chat a week. People will relax around you.

resource.heading: The coworker you are
resource.text:
Yeon: You're the expert and the listener. People ask you how things work and tell you how they feel.

Bom: Generous with both.

Guard your focus time. Being everyone's resource is a full-time job you never applied for.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Help desk and therapist, both unpaid. Close the door sometimes.

spring.heading: Your natural season at work
spring.text:
Spring-born, your natural season is the start. New projects, new teams, first-quarter momentum.

Bom: You're at your best when something is beginning. Use those months for launches and big asks.

Yeon: Schedule the maintenance work for when your interest dips. It will dip.

Bom: Next page: how you burn out. Spring people do it in a very specific way.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Big asks at the beginning of things. That's your window.

summer.heading: Your natural season at work
summer.text:
Summer-born, your natural season is full speed. Conferences, launches, everything at once.

Yeon: You thrive in intensity. Then you crash in a heap.

Bom: Book a real break right after your busiest stretch. Before it starts, so nobody can steal it.

Yeon: Next page: burnout. You already know where this is going.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Busy season first, real break right after. Book both now.

autumn.heading: Your natural season at work
autumn.text:
Autumn-born, your natural season is review and harvest. Closing projects, cleaning up processes, judging what worked.

Bom: You're excellent at finishing.

Yeon: Finishing is less glamorous than launching, so nobody claps. Make it visible anyway.

Bom: Next page: how you burn out, and how you come back.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Finishers get no confetti. Send the "it's done" email anyway.

winter.heading: Your natural season at work
winter.text:
Winter-born, your natural season is planning and depth. Research, strategy, quiet prep before anyone else starts.

Bom: You think best when things are calm. Protect the quiet weeks. That's where your best ideas live.

Yeon: Next page: burnout. Yours is quieter than most. That's what makes it sneaky.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Quiet weeks are your idea factory. Guard them.

earth.heading: Your natural season at work
earth.text:
Born in the Earth days between seasons, your natural season is the transition. Handovers, reorgs, new systems replacing old.

Bom: You stay steady when everyone else feels unsettled.

Yeon: Volunteer for transition projects. You're better at them than most people, and most people know it.

Bom: Next page: burnout, and your way back from it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Reorg incoming? Raise your hand. You're built for it.

output.heading: What disappears first when you burn out
output.text:
Your chart is short on its output element, so expression goes first. No ideas shared, no jokes, no "how are you really".

Yeon: Colleagues may not notice until it's serious. You're very good at seeming fine.

Bom: Tell one person early: "I'm running low." Saying it is exactly the output your chart is missing.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: "I'm running low." Say it to one person this week.

wealth.heading: What disappears first when you burn out
wealth.text:
Your chart is short on its wealth element, so motivation for results goes first. You still do the work. You stop caring where it leads.

Bom: Reconnect with one small goal you actually want. Even a tiny one.

Yeon: Purpose is your fastest fuel. Caffeine is a distant second.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: One tiny goal you actually want. That's the refuel.

power.heading: What disappears first when you burn out
power.text:
Your chart is short on its power element, so structure goes first. Days dissolve, tasks pile up unsorted, everything feels equally urgent.

Yeon: Your to-do list becomes a to-do novel.

Bom: Rebuild the frame. Fixed hours. A short daily list. One thing finished before noon.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Fixed hours, short list, one thing done by noon.

resource.heading: What disappears first when you burn out
resource.text:
Your chart is short on its resource element, so support goes first. Or rather, you stop accepting it.

Bom: You isolate and push through alone.

Yeon: Let someone help with one specific thing. Not "I'm fine". One thing.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Not "I'm fine". Name one thing someone can help with.

none.heading: What disappears first when you burn out
none.text:
All five elements show up in your chart, so burnout has no single front door for you.

Bom: It creeps in through whichever part of life you've neglected longest.

Yeon: Check the basics weekly. Sleep, people, movement, meaning. The one you've been skipping is the door.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Sleep, people, movement, meaning. The skipped one is your weak spot.

yang.heading: Your work rhythm: yang, outward
yang.text:
Your Day Master is yang, the outward half of saju's pair. You push forward in visible bursts. Big efforts, public commitments, decisive moves.

Bom: You recover by changing scene. Stuck? Go outside, switch projects, talk it through with someone.

Yeon: Movement unsticks you. Sitting there glaring at the screen does not.

Bom: Next page: feedback. Taking it, giving it, surviving it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Stuck? Move. Different room, different task, different person.

yin.heading: Your work rhythm: yin, inward
yin.text:
Your Day Master is yin, the inward half of saju's pair. Steady, thoughtful progress, often invisible until it's done.

Bom: You recover by going inward. Stuck? Close the door, write it down, sleep on it.

Yeon: Quiet unsticks you. Brainstorms with nine people do not.

Bom: Next page: feedback. The bit everyone dreads.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Stuck? Close the door and sleep on it.

strong.heading: How you take criticism, honestly
strong.text:
A strong chart takes criticism with a straight back and a shield already half raised.

Yeon: Your first instinct is to defend. Your second instinct is also to defend.

Bom: One rule: in the meeting, only ask questions. Defend tomorrow, if you still need to.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Questions only in the room. The defence can wait a day.

weak.heading: How you take criticism, honestly
weak.text:
A light chart takes criticism into the body. Hot face, sinking stomach, a night of replaying.

Bom: That reaction is normal for you. It doesn't mean the feedback was devastating.

Yeon: Write down the actual words that were said. They're usually much kinder than the version playing in your head.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your head's version is harsher than the real one. Check the wording.

wood.heading: Where you'd work best
wood.text:
Your balancing element is Wood, so your ideal workspace has growth in it. Plants, daylight, trees outside if you're lucky, a role with room to expand.

Bom: Standing desks, walking meetings and a shelf of things you're learning all count.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Wood workspace: daylight, plants, walking meetings.

fire.heading: Where you'd work best
fire.text:
Your balancing element is Fire, so your ideal workspace is bright and alive. Good light, energetic people, somewhere your work gets seen.

Yeon: Open plan suits you, as long as there's one room you can escape to for an hour.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Fire workspace: bright, buzzing, one escape room.

earth.heading: Where you'd work best
earth.text:
Your balancing element is Earth, so your ideal workspace is stable and comfortable. Same desk every day, a good chair, a kitchen with real food, a team that sticks around.

Yeon: Hot-desking is your personal nightmare. Every morning a new chair. No.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Earth workspace: your desk, your chair, real food.

metal.heading: Where you'd work best
metal.text:
Your balancing element is Metal, so your ideal workspace is clean and ordered. Tidy desk, clear systems, good tools, very little clutter of any kind.

Bom: Minimal setups help you think.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Metal workspace: tidy desk, good tools, nothing extra.

water.heading: Where you'd work best
water.text:
Your balancing element is Water, so your ideal workspace is flexible. Remote days, a quiet corner, travel now and then, freedom over when you work.

Yeon: Bonus points for anywhere near actual water.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Water workspace: flexible hours, a quiet corner, a view if possible.

rat.heading: Your Friday ritual (end of reading, start of weekend)
rat.text:
With the Rat under you, end the week by tying off loose threads. Three quick replies you've been avoiding, then out the door.

Bom: That's the reading. You're not hard to work with. You just work in a very specific way, and now you know it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Three dodged replies, sent. Door. Weekend.

ox.heading: Your Friday ritual (end of reading, start of weekend)
ox.text:
With the Ox under you, end the week with the tidy-desk routine and the same comforting dinner every Friday.

Bom: That's the reading. Steady isn't boring. Steady is why everything around you keeps standing.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Tidy desk, same dinner. Ritual complete.

tiger.heading: Your Friday ritual (end of reading, start of weekend)
tiger.text:
With the Tiger under you, end the week with something physical and slightly bold. A hike, a climbing gym, a trip you booked at 4pm.

Bom: That's the reading. Bring that same nerve into Monday's meeting.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Physical, bold, a little reckless. Perfect Friday.

rabbit.heading: Your Friday ritual (end of reading, start of weekend)
rabbit.text:
With the Rabbit under you, end the week somewhere pretty with someone gentle. A café, a gallery, a good friend.

Bom: That's the reading. Gentle places make you brilliant. Choose more of them, at work too.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Somewhere pretty, someone soft. That's the reset.

dragon.heading: Your Friday ritual (end of reading, start of weekend)
dragon.text:
With the Dragon under you, end the week by writing down next week's big idea. Then celebrate like it already worked.

Bom: That's the reading. The big plan you keep private? Tell one more person this month.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Write the big idea. Celebrate in advance.

snake.heading: Your Friday ritual (end of reading, start of weekend)
snake.text:
With the Snake under you, end the week quietly. A long bath, a thriller, nobody asking you anything.

Bom: That's the reading. You see more than you say. Say a little more next week.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Bath, thriller, phone face down.

horse.heading: Your Friday ritual (end of reading, start of weekend)
horse.text:
With the Horse under you, end the week moving. A run, a dance class, or a night out with your loudest friends.

Bom: That's the reading. You need motion. Build a job that lets you have it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Run, dance, loud friends. Monday can wait.

goat.heading: Your Friday ritual (end of reading, start of weekend)
goat.text:
With the Goat under you, end the week making something by hand. Cooking, drawing, a small craft. Anything that isn't a screen.

Bom: That's the reading. Your softness is a skill. Put it somewhere it's valued.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Hands busy, screen off. Proper Friday.

monkey.heading: Your Friday ritual (end of reading, start of weekend)
monkey.text:
With the Monkey under you, end the week with a game, a puzzle or a gadget you're about to take apart.

Bom: That's the reading. Bored means you've outgrown it. Go find the harder puzzle.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: One puzzle, one gadget, zero instructions read.

rooster.heading: Your Friday ritual (end of reading, start of weekend)
rooster.text:
With the Rooster under you, end the week by planning a perfect Saturday and dressing up for no reason.

Bom: That's the reading. Your standards are a gift. Aim a little of that care at yourself.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Saturday planned, outfit chosen, nobody to impress.

dog.heading: Your Friday ritual (end of reading, start of weekend)
dog.text:
With the Dog under you, end the week with your oldest friends. The ones who knew you before this job.

Bom: That's the reading. You defend everyone at work. Make sure someone defends your weekends.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Old friends, zero work talk. Rule enforced.

pig.heading: Your Friday ritual (end of reading, start of weekend)
pig.text:
With the Pig under you, end the week with a feast, a nap and absolutely no alarm set for Saturday.

Bom: That's the reading. You give generously. Keep some of it for you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Feast, nap, alarm off. Glorious.

spring.heading: When your year peaks
spring.text:
Spring-born, you tend to peak when the days get longer. Late winter into spring.

Bom: That's the window for pitches, new roles and big conversations with your manager.

Yeon: In the heavy months of late autumn, lower the bar a little. Finish things. Don't start empires.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Longer days, bigger asks. That's your timing.

summer.heading: When your year peaks
summer.text:
Summer-born, you tend to run strongest in the bright, busy months.

Bom: Use that window for the projects that need the most push and visibility.

Yeon: In winter, plan, learn and rest instead of forcing launches. Your spark comes back with the light.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Launch in the light, plan in the dark months.

autumn.heading: When your year peaks
autumn.text:
Autumn-born, your sharpest months are the crisp ones, when the year turns toward results and deadlines.

Bom: Schedule your hardest analytical work and your reviews then.

Yeon: Spring chaos feels scattered to you. Use it for exploring, not deciding.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Hard thinking in crisp months. Exploring in spring.

winter.heading: When your year peaks
winter.text:
Winter-born, you often think most clearly when the world slows down.

Bom: The quiet weeks around the end of the year are gold for strategy, writing and deep work.

Yeon: Summer's social whirl drains you faster than most. Protect a few quiet evenings, even in July.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: The quiet end of the year is your gold. Plan around it.

earth.heading: When your year peaks
earth.text:
Born in the Earth days, you do best in the in-between weeks, when one season or project hands over to the next.

Bom: You're steady during change.

Yeon: Volunteer to plan the next phase while everyone else is still finishing the last one. Sneaky. Effective.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Handover weeks are your sweet spot.

peer.heading: How you give feedback
peer.text:
With {heavy_el} turning up most in your chart, you give feedback as an equal. Direct, frank, a little competitive.

Yeon: Works great with peers. Lands like a brick on juniors.

Bom: With anyone junior, add one sentence on how you'd help them fix it.

Yeon: Next page: the job that actually fits you. I made a list.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Frank with peers, plus a helping hand for juniors.

output.heading: How you give feedback
output.text:
With {heavy_el} turning up most in your chart, your feedback is vivid and full of ideas for how it could be better.

Yeon: So full that the person drowns somewhere around idea six.

Bom: Pick your favourite idea. Save the rest for another day.

Yeon: Next page: the job that actually fits you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Twelve suggestions is a flood. Pick the best one.

wealth.heading: How you give feedback
wealth.text:
With {heavy_el} turning up most in your chart, your feedback is practical and results-focused. What needs to change to hit the goal.

Bom: Clear. Useful.

Yeon: Add one line about their effort, not just the output. They're people, not a dashboard.

Bom: Next page: the job that fits you. Yeon has opinions.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Results-focused is good. Mention the effort too.

power.heading: How you give feedback
power.text:
With {heavy_el} turning up most in your chart, your feedback is structured and fair, often pointing to standards and rules.

Bom: It's credible.

Yeon: It can also sound like a court verdict. Turn one statement into a question: "What would you change here?"

Bom: Next page: the job that actually fits you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Swap one verdict for a question. Watch them lean in.

resource.heading: How you give feedback
resource.text:
With {heavy_el} turning up most in your chart, your feedback is thoughtful and explanatory. Basically a lesson with slides.

Bom: People learn a lot.

Yeon: And sometimes miss the bottom line entirely. Say the main point first, then teach.

Bom: Next page: the job that fits you, according to your chart.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Bottom line first. Then the lecture.

output.heading: The one skill worth borrowing
output.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible pillars, so the skill worth borrowing is self-presentation. Talking about your work, demos, writing up what you did.

Bom: It won't come naturally. It's learnable, like a language.

Yeon: Practise on low-stakes updates first. Nobody remembers the Tuesday team email.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Self-presentation is learnable. Practise on small updates.

wealth.heading: The one skill worth borrowing
wealth.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible pillars, so the skill worth borrowing is negotiation. Asking for resources, scope and recognition.

Bom: Read one good book on it.

Yeon: Then ask for one small thing a month. Small asks build the muscle.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Negotiation is a muscle. One small ask a month.

power.heading: The one skill worth borrowing
power.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible pillars, so the skill worth borrowing is self-management. Calendars, deadlines, systems that keep you going when motivation dips.

Yeon: Tools are your friends. One tool. Not nine productivity apps.

Bom: Pick one system and stick with it for three months.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One system, three months. Not a new app every week.

resource.heading: The one skill worth borrowing
resource.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible pillars, so the skill worth borrowing is learning on purpose. Courses, mentors, reading.

Bom: You learn by doing, which is fast but patchy.

Yeon: Fill the gaps deliberately. You've been winging one particular thing for years. You know which.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You learn by doing. Fill the holes doing leaves.

none.heading: The one skill worth borrowing
none.text:
All five elements present, so no glaring gap. The skill worth borrowing is focus: choosing what not to do.

Bom: Range is a gift until it scatters you.

Yeon: Write a short "not doing this year" list. It's the most freeing document you'll ever make.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: A "not doing this year" list. Range needs edges.

gap-wood.text:
Minute four: "So what are we actually trying to decide?" The meeting suddenly has a spine.

Bom: You defend whoever isn't in the room. Someone criticises an absent colleague and you say "let's ask them first".

Yeon: Then the decision you cared about gets made and you leave. Mentally. Laptop open, planning next steps.

Bom: Others notice the second hour you.

Yeon: Give yourself the closing job: summarise the actions. Pines are great at standing tall at the start. Stay rooted to the last item.

Bom: Next page: where you actually are right now. Your answers gave you away.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You give meetings a backbone. Stay till the last agenda item.

gap-wood.heading: You in a meeting (Yeon took minutes)

eul-wood.text:
You read the room before you say a word. Who's tense. Who's bored. Who's about to get steamrolled.

Bom: When you finally speak, it's the compromise everyone suddenly agrees with. Rarely credited by name.

Yeon: And sometimes the moment never comes. You leave with the idea unsaid and mention it in the hallway, where it doesn't count.

Bom: Speak once in the first ten minutes. Even a small question.

Yeon: It plants you in the conversation. Vines need an anchor before they climb.

Bom: Next page: where you really are right now. Honestly.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: The hallway is not a meeting. Say it in the room.

eul-wood.heading: You in a meeting (Yeon took minutes)

byeong-fire.text:
You arrive with a story, crack the first joke and push for the bold option. On a dull Tuesday that's a public service.

Bom: People leave your meetings more awake than they came in.

Yeon: Airtime check, though. You filled forty of the fifty minutes. Again.

Bom: After you speak, name someone. "Mina, you know this better than me. What am I missing?"

Yeon: You'll still be the brightest person in the room. You'll also be the one who made everyone else visible. That's the senior move.

Bom: Next page: where you actually are right now. Your answers said a lot.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Forty of fifty minutes. Pass the mic.

byeong-fire.heading: You in a meeting (Yeon took minutes)

jeong-fire.text:
Quiet for twenty minutes. Then: "Who is this actually for?" The room goes silent.

Bom: You notice the human side of a plan. The customer who'll be confused. The colleague who'll get stuck with the extra work.

Yeon: Then someone sighs dismissively and you replay that sigh on the whole commute.

Bom: After hard meetings, a small ritual. Walk to the coffee machine. Two lines in a notebook about what was actually decided.

Yeon: The candle stays steady if the draft has somewhere to go.

Bom: Next page: where you really are right now, according to you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: One sigh across the table and you've written a novel about it by 6pm.

jeong-fire.heading: You in a meeting (Yeon took minutes)

mu-earth.text:
First half: silence. Second half: you summarise the whole mess in three sentences and suggest a way forward.

Bom: People defer to you. Partly because you sound certain. Partly because you usually are.

Yeon: Then you decide something's wrong and every new argument bounces off. Colleagues stop trying.

Bom: Leave one window open. Say it aloud: "What would change my mind here?"

Yeon: Mountains are trusted for being stable. They're loved when they turn out to be listening.

Bom: Next page: where you really are right now.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Three sentences, meeting saved. Now leave one window open.

mu-earth.heading: You in a meeting (Yeon took minutes)

gi-earth.text:
You brought the snacks, took the notes and remembered the action item from last month. Meetings work because you're in them.

Bom: You notice who hasn't spoken and gently bring them in.

Yeon: Then a task floats in the air with no owner and your hand goes up. By Friday you're doing four people's follow-ups.

Bom: Count to five before you volunteer.

Yeon: Often someone else grabs it in the pause. If nobody does, you'll know it truly needs you.

Bom: Next page: where you really are right now. Your answers were honest. We noticed.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: One, two, three, four, five. See? Someone else took it.

gi-earth.heading: You in a meeting (Yeon took minutes)

gyeong-metal.text:
Minute six: you've found the weak point. Minute seven: you've said it. Plainly.

Bom: Decisions happen faster with you there. Projects dodge expensive mistakes. Leaders bring you in to stress-test ideas.

Yeon: The angle of the blade, though. You say the right thing and the person who proposed it stays defensive for an hour.

Bom: Try a real question: "I like where this is going. What happens if the supplier is late?"

Yeon: Same point. The person stays on your side. Swords are most useful when people are glad to see them.

Bom: Next page: where you really are right now. Yeon read your answers twice.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Same point, phrased as a question. Fewer enemies by Friday.

gyeong-metal.heading: You in a meeting (Yeon took minutes)

sin-metal.text:
Slide nine has a typo. You saw it before the presenter finished slide two.

Bom: The number in the summary doesn't match. The deadline doesn't add up. You catch all of it.

Yeon: Colleagues tease you. Then they quietly send you their decks before big presentations.

Bom: The miss is the big picture. You have a sharp view on strategy and hold it until you're sure.

Yeon: Share it at eighty percent. A clear opinion a bit early beats a perfect one after the decision.

Bom: Next page: where you really are right now. Your answers were very precise.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You caught the typo. Now say the strategy thing you've been sitting on.

sin-metal.heading: You in a meeting (Yeon took minutes)

im-water.text:
"This is the same problem sales had last year." Silence. Then everyone rethinks everything.

Bom: You connect things nobody connected. Your best meetings have a whiteboard and no fixed agenda.

Yeon: Status updates, though. You visibly leave your body. Colleagues can see it.

Bom: If you can't avoid them, give yourself a job. Track the decisions. Spot links to other teams.

Yeon: Oceans stay interested when they have a current to follow. Give your mind one, even in the weekly sync.

Bom: Next page: where you really are right now. Stay with us.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Status update in progress. Your soul: on a beach somewhere.

im-water.heading: You in a meeting (Yeon took minutes)

gye-water.text:
"I think we're all a bit worried about the timeline." The room exhales. You said what everyone felt.

Bom: You sense undercurrents. Unspoken tension. The person who disagrees but won't say so.

Yeon: Excellent facilitator, whatever your title. Then you spend the afternoon wondering if you sounded silly.

Bom: You didn't. Write down one thing you contributed after each meeting. Evidence.

Yeon: Rain doesn't measure itself drop by drop. It just notices, a month later, that everything grew.

Bom: Next page: where you really are right now. Gently.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You said the thing everyone felt. Write it down as evidence.

gye-water.heading: You in a meeting (Yeon took minutes)

gap-wood.text:
"What's your weakness?" Your face, every time: personally offended.

Bom: You come across as solid and principled. Interviewers can picture you leading by the second answer.

Yeon: You hate looking anything less than upright. So have a true answer ready. "I take on too much responsibility," plus one real example of delegating.

Bom: Choosing between offers, ask: "Where could this role be in two years?"

Yeon: A pine with no room to grow is a very frustrated pine. Pick the clearest upward line, not the shiniest title.

Bom: Last chapter next: your best week at work, built from your chart.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Shiny title, no growth path? Hard pass.

gap-wood.heading: You in a job interview (Yeon is on the panel)

eul-wood.text:
They like you within four minutes. You mirror their tone, find common ground, tell a lovely story about collaboration.

Yeon: Then you say "we did" fourteen times and they can't tell what was yours.

Bom: Practise three "I did" sentences before every interview. Use all three.

Yeon: Choosing between offers, look at the people more than the package.

Bom: Ask to meet one future teammate before signing. Ten minutes of coffee tells you more than the job description.

Yeon: Last chapter next. Your best week at work. Bring a pen.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: "We" is generous. In interviews, say "I".

eul-wood.heading: You in a job interview (Yeon is on the panel)

byeong-fire.text:
Interviewers walk out of your interview smiling. Some of them forget to ask the hard questions.

Yeon: The trap is you, excited, agreeing to responsibilities you'd never choose on a calm day.

Bom: Before you say yes to a new scope, ask for a day to think.

Yeon: Choosing between offers, pick visibility. Client-facing, real launches, a company proud of its work.

Bom: Ask how success gets recognised there. Then listen very carefully to the answer.

Yeon: Last chapter next. Your best week. Spoiler: it has an audience.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Excited yes, regretful Tuesday. Ask for a day first.

byeong-fire.heading: You in a job interview (Yeon is on the panel)

jeong-fire.text:
The interviewer looks cold and you shrink by one size per question.

Bom: You're thoughtful and sincere. You don't oversell. People sense the depth.

Yeon: But you tune to their mood too much. Pick one story you're proud of and tell it fully, whatever their face is doing.

Bom: Choosing between offers, pick meaning and a decent manager. Your boss is your shelter.

Yeon: Ask how they give feedback and what happens when someone makes a mistake. That answer predicts your Tuesdays better than the salary band.

Bom: Last chapter next: your best week at work.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Their face is not your scorecard. Tell the whole story.

jeong-fire.heading: You in a job interview (Yeon is on the panel)

mu-earth.text:
You seem like someone who'll still be there in five years. Interviewers find that very attractive.

Yeon: Risk: so calm they wonder if you want anything at all.

Bom: Mention one thing you want to build, concretely. Let them see the drive under the calm.

Yeon: Choosing between offers, ask how long people on the team have stayed.

Bom: Long tenure usually means leadership that keeps its word. That's your kind of ground.

Yeon: Last chapter next: your best week at work. Low drama, I promise.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Calm is great. Show them one thing you'd build.

mu-earth.heading: You in a job interview (Yeon is on the panel)

gi-earth.text:
You researched the company, remembered the interviewer's name and asked about their weekend. They love you.

Yeon: Then you describe your biggest achievement like it was a small favour.

Bom: Bring numbers. "I organised onboarding for forty new hires" sounds as big as it was.

Yeon: Choosing between offers, ask how the team supports people in busy seasons.

Bom: A vague answer means you'd become everyone's unpaid helper there. Pick the place that has a watering plan.

Yeon: Last chapter next. Your best week. Someone finally thanks you in it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Humble is lovely. Invisible isn't. Bring the numbers.

gi-earth.heading: You in a job interview (Yeon is on the panel)

gyeong-metal.text:
You answer exactly the question asked. Real example. No padding. Done in ninety seconds.

Yeon: Many interviewers love it. Some write "intimidating" in their notes.

Bom: Add one warm moment. A colleague you helped. A laugh about a project that went sideways.

Yeon: Choosing between offers, ask: "Who decides when we disagree?"

Bom: If nobody can answer, that's a role where your sword spends its days cutting fog.

Yeon: Last chapter next. Your best week. It involves a climbing wall.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One warm story. It shows the person behind the edge.

gyeong-metal.heading: You in a job interview (Yeon is on the panel)

sin-metal.text:
Good outfit, good portfolio, crisp answers. You're grading every word as it leaves your mouth.

Yeon: Which makes you seem a bit guarded. Perfectly guarded.

Bom: Let one answer be imperfect and personal. What you love about your field. It makes the polish feel human.

Yeon: Choosing between offers, ask to see something the team made recently.

Bom: Your reaction in the first five seconds tells you whether you belong there.

Yeon: Last chapter next: your best week at work. It ends in a gallery, obviously.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Five seconds looking at their work tells you everything.

sin-metal.heading: You in a job interview (Yeon is on the panel)

im-water.text:
Twenty minutes in, you're interviewing them. They're enjoying it.

Yeon: You connect the role to big trends and ask brilliant questions. Then drift into a tangent about supply chains in 1890.

Bom: Prepare two crisp examples with clear results, so the big ideas have proof attached.

Yeon: Choosing between offers, ask what a typical week looks like.

Bom: If every week sounds the same, keep looking, or negotiate a side project from day one.

Yeon: Last chapter next. Your best week. It has a walk in it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Identical weeks forever? That's a tank, not an ocean.

im-water.heading: You in a job interview (Yeon is on the panel)

gye-water.text:
You figure out what the interviewer really cares about by question two. They don't even notice.

Yeon: Then nerves turn your answers into mist.

Bom: Write your three key points on a card. Glance at it before you walk in. Clear rain beats fog.

Yeon: Choosing between offers, notice everything. How the receptionist was treated. Whether anyone laughed in the hallway.

Bom: Your read of a place is usually right. Trust it more than the brochure.

Yeon: Last chapter next. Your best week, built for you.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: The hallway told you everything. Trust it.

gye-water.heading: You in a job interview (Yeon is on the panel)

strong.heading: You and your boss (Yeon has notes)
strong.text:
You don't love being managed. You respect competent, fair bosses and quietly test the rest.

Yeon: You've disagreed with a boss in front of the whole team. More than once. You'd do it again.

Bom: That earns respect or starts a cold war, depending on the boss.

The smarter play is private disagreement, public support. Raise the objection one-on-one, with a better option. If the decision stands, back it in front of the team. Your autonomy grows faster when they trust you won't undercut them.

Bom: Strong charts often end up leading. Be the kind of report you'd want to have.

Yeon: Next page: your elements, and what they do to you at work. One is too loud. One is missing.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Disagree in private, back them in public. Autonomy follows.

weak.heading: You and your boss (Yeon has notes)
weak.text:
A short email from your boss and you're reviewing your entire life.

Bom: A skipped one-on-one, a distracted face, and you're wondering what you did. Usually nothing. Bosses are busy and grumpy for their own reasons.

Yeon: Protect yourself with structure. A regular fifteen-minute check-in every two weeks.

Bring a short list: what you did, what's blocking you, one question. Once a quarter ask, "Is there anything you'd like me to do differently?" The real answer is usually small, and much better than the imagined one.

Bom: Next page: your elements at work. What you've got too much of, and what's missing.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Fifteen minutes every two weeks, with a list. The spiral shrinks.

wood.heading: How you come back
wood.text:
Wood rebalances you, so the way back starts with something growing. Not another work goal. Something small and alive.

Bom: A new route on your walk. A beginner's class in anything. A plant you actually water.

Yeon: Tiny progress outside work rebuilds what the job drained. Give it three weeks before you judge it.

Bom: Next page: your blind spot. Yeon's favourite chapter.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Grow something small. Judge it in three weeks, not three days.

fire.heading: How you come back
fire.text:
Fire rebalances you, so the way back starts with warmth and people. Burnout tells you to hide. Do the opposite, gently.

Bom: One dinner with a friend who makes you laugh. A concert. A sunny afternoon outside.

Yeon: Not lying in a dark room scrolling. That's not rest, that's a screensaver.

Bom: One warm evening a week. Then next page: the blind spot.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Burnout says hide. Book one evening with your funniest friend.

earth.heading: How you come back
earth.text:
Earth rebalances you, so the way back starts with routine and the body's basics.

Bom: Regular meals. Same bedtime. A walk at the same hour.

Yeon: Boring. Exactly what your system needs after chaos.

Bom: Cook something simple on Sunday for the week. Steady structure gives your mind solid ground again. Next page: your blind spot.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Same bedtime, Sunday cooking. Boring is the medicine.

metal.heading: How you come back
metal.text:
Metal rebalances you, so the way back starts with cutting. Unsubscribe, decline, delete the app, clear the desk.

Yeon: Your burnout is usually forty-seven open loops.

Bom: List every commitment. Cross off three you can drop or delay.

Yeon: An emptier calendar will do more for you than any spa weekend. Next page: the blind spot. Sharpen up.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: List everything. Cross off three. Breathe.

water.heading: How you come back
water.text:
Water rebalances you, so the way back starts with stillness and sleep. Real rest, not productive rest.

Bom: A morning with no plans. A long bath. Reading something with zero connection to work.

Yeon: A muddy glass clears when you stop shaking it. Stop shaking it.

Bom: A few unstructured hours a week. Then turn the page to your blind spot.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Stop shaking the glass. Let it settle.

wood.heading: Your emails, honestly
wood.text:
Yeon: Subject line with a verb. Clear ask. A next step and a date. Then the "one more thing" paragraph that adds three projects.

Bom: One email, one direction. Send the extras later.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your "one more thing" paragraph is a whole second email.

fire.heading: Your emails, honestly
fire.text:
Yeon: Exclamation marks. So many exclamation marks. "Thanks so much!!" "Love this!!"

Bom: Your warmth comes through. Just keep one sentence that says what you need.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Warm emails are great. Put the ask in the first line.

earth.heading: Your emails, honestly
earth.text:
Bom: Thorough, clear, every detail covered. People trust your emails.

Yeon: People also scroll for a while. Bullet points exist. Use them.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Three bullet points beat three paragraphs. Every time.

metal.heading: Your emails, honestly
metal.text:
Yeon: Short. Precise. Occasionally terrifying. "Per my last email" is your love language.

Bom: Add one warm line at the start. It doesn't weaken the point. It gets it read.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: "Per my last email" is technically a threat.

water.heading: Your emails, honestly
water.text:
Bom: Full of ideas. Interesting. Connected thoughts.

Yeon: Also no clear ask. People read it twice and still don't know what you want from them.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: End every email with one clear question.

student.speaker: bom
student.text: Still studying. Perfect time to learn how you work, before a boss decides it for you.

early.speaker: yeon
early.text: Early in your career. So you're still saying "happy to help!" in emails you'd like to set on fire.

mid.speaker: yeon
mid.text: A few years in. Long enough to know the job. Not long enough to stop rewriting your Slack messages three times.

lead.speaker: bom
lead.text: Leading people. So now it's not just how you work. It's how a whole team feels on Monday morning.

between.speaker: bom
between.text: Between jobs. Honestly a great moment for this. You get to pick the next one on purpose.

unsaid.speaker: yeon
unsaid.text: You skipped where you are. Fine. Your birthday tells me how you work. Your face on Sunday night tells me the rest.

meetings.speaker: yeon
meetings.text: Endless meetings drain you. "This could have been an email" lives in your head rent-free.

unclear.speaker: yeon
unclear.text: Unclear goals drain you. You can do anything. You just need someone to say what "anything" is.

people.speaker: bom
people.text: Difficult people drain you. That's not you being sensitive. That's you paying a tax nobody else sees.

boredom.speaker: yeon
boredom.text: Boredom drains you. Same task, same day, same lunch. Your brain is filing a complaint.

unsaid.speaker: bom
unsaid.text: No answer on the draining part. We'll find it anyway. It's usually the thing you complain about on Thursdays.

strength_titles.strong: Your blind spot: you push too hard
strength_titles.weak: Your blind spot: you give too much

gyeong-metal.how-you-work:
You work like a blade: you find the problem and cut straight to it.

Bom: You get results others are too scared to chase.

Yeon: You also make people cry in reviews. Not on purpose. You just said the true thing with no cushion.

Bom: Your directness is valuable. Add one warm sentence before the sharp one.
gyeong-metal.how-you-lead:
Bom: They'd follow you because everybody knows exactly where they stand. The mission, the standards, the consequences.

Yeon: In a crisis, people want you in charge. On a quiet Tuesday, slightly less.

You protect your team fiercely from outside chaos. Nobody gets thrown under a bus on your watch.

Bom: The edge cuts inward sometimes. Feedback that's accurate and wounding. Pushing people past what's sustainable.

Yeon: Some of your best people may leave quietly, because they never once felt appreciated.

Bom: Praise specifically and publicly, as often as you correct. You don't have to lower the bar. Just tell people when they clear it.
gyeong-metal.coworkers:
"There's a hole in this plan." In the meeting. In front of everyone. While the plan's author is presenting.

Bom: People trust your word completely.

Yeon: Some of them are also slightly scared of you.

Bom: Your clashes are with indecisive, political or lazy colleagues. You don't hide the contempt well.

Yeon: Sensitive colleagues hear your directness as aggression. You hear their sensitivity as a delay.

Bom: Choose the setting: hard truths in private, one kind sentence first, listen without interrupting. Same honesty. Better door.
gyeong-metal.burnout:
Every problem is a battle. Every battle is yours. And then the blade goes dull.

Bom: You charge at every crisis and refuse to look weak.

Yeon: Warning signs: rage over a calendar invite, cynicism about the entire organisation, insomnia, a growing belief that nobody else is competent.

Bom: Recovery means stepping off the battlefield. Exercise that exhausts you in a good way.

Yeon: A hobby with clear rules and nothing at stake.

Bom: And the hard one: let someone else handle a crisis, even if they do it differently.
gyeong-metal.job-vibe:
Give you a clear target and the authority to hit it. Then step back.

Bom: Decisive, high-stakes, results-driven. Clear wins, real consequences.

Yeon: A consensus-heavy place where nothing gets decided would turn you into the person sighing loudly on every call.

Bom: Real problems, real stakes. That's where your edge becomes a gift.

gyeong-metal.speaker: bom
gyeong-metal.text: The sword at work. Direct, decisive, gets it done.

gyeong-metal.speaker: yeon
gyeong-metal.text: Your manager schedules you last in meetings. For everyone's safety.

gyeong-metal.speaker: bom
gyeong-metal.text: You cut through the noise. People trust your honesty.

gyeong-metal.speaker: yeon
gyeong-metal.text: You fixed something nobody asked you to fix. Again. Count to five next time.

gyeong-metal.speaker: bom
gyeong-metal.text: Choose the room first. Then the words.

gyeong-metal.speaker: yeon
gyeong-metal.text: Hand the next fire to someone else. It gets handled. Differently. Fine.

spring.intro: A blade born in spring, surrounded by things to cut. You see what needs doing and you do it, preferably before anyone has finished explaining. Efficient. Also sometimes the reason the meeting went badly.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You solved their problem. They wanted a hug. Classic.

summer.intro: A sword forged in summer. Heat everywhere, so you were shaped by pressure: deadlines, expectations, people who pushed. It made you strong and principled. It also made you assume love is a test you can fail.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You don't have to pass anything. You're already loved.

earth.intro: A sword still in the stone. Born in the soil weeks, so you were held, fed and protected before you were ever swung. That gives you patience most Swords lack, and a stubborn streak made of actual rock.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Patient, until you're not. Then it's a sword.

autumn.intro: A sword born in autumn, metal's own season. Double steel. Loyal to the bone, blunt as a brick, and fair in a way that scares people. You'd fight anyone for a friend, and tell that friend exactly where they went wrong on the way home.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You'd take a bullet for a friend. Then critique their aim.

winter.intro: A blade in winter. Cold, clear, and sharpened by thinking. You say less than other Swords, but when you speak it lands like a verdict. People quote you back to yourself years later.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your words stay with people. Choose the kind ones too.

gyeong-metal.strong:
Strong chart, Sword. You win most battles.

Yeon: Including several that didn't need fighting. The printer. The font policy. The guy in finance.

Bom: Your drive and confidence carry teams through things that would break others.

Yeon: The blind spot: you're so used to winning that you stop asking which fights are worth it.

Bom: Before you engage, ask: will this matter in a month?

Yeon: If not, sheath it. The guy in finance will survive.
gyeong-metal.weak:
Light chart, Sword. A blade still being shaped.

Bom: Feedback forms you. You take it seriously and act on it fast.

Yeon: Including feedback from people who have no business shaping anyone.

Bom: Choose mentors who sharpen without breaking you.

Yeon: Two or three names. The rest go in the "noted, ignored" folder.

Bom: You get stronger every time you're tested. Make sure the tests are fair.

feedback.text:
You'd rather be told bluntly than handled. Vague feedback makes you want to flip a table.

Yeon: You argue back in the meeting. Then you quietly fix it overnight and never mention it.

Bom: The feedback that works on you: specific, fast, unpadded.

Yeon: Giving it is where your blade shows. Accurate, fast, and people feel cut.

Bom: Start with what's working. Be specific about the one thing to change. Ask how they see it before you leave.

Yeon: Your honesty is valuable. Delivered with care, it changes careers.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Argued in the meeting, fixed it by morning. Never admitted either.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Accurate isn't the same as heard. Ask them how they see it.

best-week.text:
One real problem. One owner. You.

Bom: Monday, a clear problem with your name on it.

Yeon: Tuesday and Wednesday, you solve it decisively and cancel two pointless meetings on the way. Hero behaviour.

Bom: Thursday, you tell a team member exactly what they did well and watch them light up.

Yeon: Friday, measurable results, nothing half finished, then the gym or the climbing wall. Work left behind completely.

Bom: One problem solved, one person recognised, a hard workout to close the week.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Two meetings cancelled. Best feeling of your quarter.

job-list.heading: Roles that tend to fit, picked by Yeon
job-list.text: Litigator, auditor, crisis or turnaround manager, emergency coordinator, engineer on critical systems, consultant, coach in competitive sport, security lead. The thread: stakes, clarity, and someone who has to make the call.

gyeong-metal.title: You told the director it was a bad idea. In the meeting. You were right.
gyeong-metal.text:
You see what's broken and you say so. Immediately. Directly. Your manager has learned to schedule you last in meetings.

Bom: You're the honest one.

Yeon: You're the honest one, and HR knows your name. Not in a bad way. Mostly.
gyeong-metal.end: Yeon: How you work is sharp. How it lands on other people is next page.

cliff.gyeong-metal: Yeon: How you lead, Sword: your team would follow you | into battle. They'd also love one meeting where you don't fix something they didn't ask you to fix.

gyeong-metal.speaker: yeon
gyeong-metal.text: Job vibe: real problems, real stakes, no politics. Office drama will make you want to quit by lunch.
